content:
The father, who had marched on, stopped in his tracks when he saw the boy and his tense, wary expression started to warmed a little immediately. Civilisation. Their people! They found it! "Friends." he repeated before glancing over his shoulder, then back to the boy when his sons arrived. "My family and me." The brothers looked like they were about to forget about all their pain and rush over to the fire. They could barely contain their relief and excitement. Gwyndolin, who stepped out of the cave after her brothers couldn't keep a sigh of relief in. "We did it...!" Gwyndolin's youngest brother groaned and Gwyndolin had to smile at his outburst. "This is the black dragon's roost, yes?" she asked, though, as she slowly stepped closer. "We came to serve and brought gifts from our homeland for the dragon and the community." The brothers already stumbled exhausted over to the fire. Gwyndolin's father stayed by her side, though. They all were exhausted but his sons could still fight, if this ended up not being the roost and instead, the people here turned out to be enemies. Gwyndolin didn't want to feel alarmed or cautious. They had been for so long. She just wanted warmth and sleep right now. Maybe some tea...but first: "What's your name? I'm Gwyndolin and that's my father, Ruhon." she told the boy. "And this is Dapple." she added with a chuckle, stroking the head of the donkey with her free hand. "Father, let's go to the fire." she coaxed and started to walk again. She spotted her brothers, warming themselves up and already chatting up people. At least they were introducing themselves, too... Gwyndolin's golden eyes gleamed when they reached the fire and she felt a shudder as the warmth touched her. Finally...by the spirits, finally. She sank on her knees, exhausted from the long journey, just like her brothers and her father. "I thought we end up dead sooner or later..." her older brother sighed. "Mh..." Gwyndolin made, almost absent minded. She didn't want to agree verbally. But yes, they would have been in a horrible situation if they wouldn't have found this community today.

The city was busy. Traders where rushing from the port, moving cargo into their stores, many people walked around to do their shopping. There were even a lot of tourists. Quite a lot of nords, a hand full of Bosmer even, though they seemed to know the area well enough. One, who spotted Elluinor, grinned at him passing by. "Y'ffre bless you!" But he didn't stop, as he was hurring into the direction of another district...with a purse in his hand. A purse that looked nordic... Well, Bosmer being Bosmer, some Nord was a purse poorer now! An elder Altmer stopped in his tracks, though and turned around to look at the stone tablet. "Well, well, well, where did you find this?" he asked intrigued. "I'd take this from your hands for ten gold and a piece of advice, young one." he said with a smile as he stroked the thin beard he was trying to grow in his age. "Though the advice is just an addition...but it will become very useful to you. What do you say?" From one of the Inns, a rather drunk Nord suddenly stumbled out of the building. "Where is that little beaver, huh?! Anyone seen a little brat with knife-ears runnin' away?!" he called. "Oh my. Always the same with this one..." The high elf in front of Elluinor said with a sigh.

The little boy's eyes beamed up more, when he got the confirmation that they were friends. He almost dropped the basket with berries he was carrying, but instead sheathed his dagger he had in the other hand to free up one of them. "Friends! Welcome!" he said excited. His expression grew solemn for a moment when she asked about the dragon and he nodded reverently. This was an important thing, he knew. A holy thing. "Come, come.. you are cold!" he said quickly then though, seeing the brothers shiver and the state of their clothes, too. "Hello Dapple" he said when she introduced the donkey though and offered his hand to the donkey to smell first before he led them over to the fire. "Mama!" he cried out joyfully while they approached already. "New survivors!" A middle-aged woman, probably nearing 40, looked up from her task when she was called and looked at her boy bringing the new faces over to their little settlement. "Oh" she made surprised first but after shortly scanning their features, she looked relieved. They were obviously from their homeland. "Be welcome" she said "Ah, here, cast off your wet clothes" she said and looked over to another boy, this one closer to Gwyn's age than the first, but still far from fully grown up - a teenager "Rosvalt, bring them blankets and furs to get comfortable. They must be worn out from the journey." she called over and the boy that had been working on one of the tents got up and vanished into the tent to soon bring out blankets and furs to make the floor around the fire more comfortable and give them something to cuddle into. He blushed faintly when he handed a blanket to Gwyndolin. She was very pretty, after all. "My apologies, most of us are working by the mountainside or hunting right now.." she said to the new arrivals. Her own belly was round - swollen with child. Probably not too far from the day it would come into this world. "Is that everyone you came with?" she asked, a little saddened. It had been only their group that had managed to evade the elves fully. Everyone else had been scattered before coming here. Survivors came in small trickles, if at all. "Ah, where are my manners.." she scolded herself. "I'm Grunhild, this is my youngest thus far, Kjer and Rosvalt my oldest." she said proudly then. "My husband, Erald, is working the stone with most other men. They will be glad for help in the days to come, once you have rested up from your journey." she said pleased to the father and brothers. She fought herself to her feet and introduced herself quietly to the donkey before she began to unload the burdens from the beast to set them aside for now. Before they could do much more than cast off whatever was wet or too uncomfortable to still wear, a young girl came over to them with a smile and handed out bowls of soup to them. It was a thin soup, stretched clearly, but it had some potatoes and carrots, leek and some wild game in there that was all thoroughly cooked and pretty much melted on the tongue. But most and for all it was warm. "More to come." she promised. "But until the others are back from their work, warm yourselves a little with this and regain some strength.." she told them and gave the men a gentle touch on the shoulder when she passed them and Gwyndolin a big smile. She was happy to have someone new in her age here.

Elluinor perked up when he saw the bosmer greeting him as he passed by without stopping. He gave a grin back to him. "Y'ffre guide you!" he replied amused. He had a good eye for detail and spotted the nordic looking purse that was definitely out of place in his hands immediately. Well! Traditions needed to be kept and taken care of! He glanced up to the Altmer that stopped to look at the tablet. He knew this was something of importance, even if he didn't know all of it. It had been heavy to lug around. He wouldn't have done that if he didn't believe this was worth something to a historian or maybe even a mage. "Near an Ayleid ruin." he answered honestly. "It was overgrown, I pried it from the vine's embrace and cleaned it up by the river." he told him. "Not sure about the origin or the language it's written in.. but I'm certain it's worth more than 10 gold." he admitted in the end with a little grin as he looked up to the Altmer. "How about 40? And if I come across more that are similar to this one, I'll know there's someone I can do good business with here and take care to bring them along when I come through here again." he suggested then. He was sure he would not pay 40. But perhaps he'd meet him closer to the middle of it and even then he'd still have doubled the initial offer. He glanced shortly over to the nord that bust out of the inn and had to smirk a little, but focused back on the Altmer and kept a watchful eye over his belongings here. "He is known here?" he assumed then. "It seems like many different people live here. I've never seen so many different races in one place." he said and couldn't contain some excitement in his voice.

"My thanks. It's been so long since we've seen a proper camp and friendly faces. My family and I, we are the only ones left from our caravan..." Gwyndolin's father said with a worn-out sigh. The exhaustion was clear. None of them would have the energy to do much for the rest of the day. When her son brought blankets and pelts, Gwyndolin just was taking off the outer coat of her clothes, which were wet from snow. "Thank you so much." she breathed and gave the boy a smile when she took the blanket from him. She wrapped it around her body and slipped closer to the fire. "Ah, we can help...once my leg's better. Got mauled by a mountain lion two nights ago and it managed to bite into my leg." Gwyn's younger brother said while the older one got up and helped up the pregnant woman. "Nice meeting you all. I am Rohal, this is my youngest son Bastan and my oldest son, Runon. And of course, my daughter Gwyndolin. We are a family of smiths, though Bastan is a very good hunter and my daughter had shown quite the talent of being a good healer." he said, just as proud as Grunhild while talking about their children. They all took off their boots and whatever was wet and got comfortable in front of the fire. Bastan's leg was well taken care of. It was bandaged and didn't seem to be bleeding but it was still painful to walk for him, so he was glad to be finally sitting. "Later, let me check your wound again." "After we slept, right?" Bastan groaned and Gwyndolin smiled at that. "You can sleep while I see to your leg." she assured him. When the girl came, though, Bastan straightened suddenly his back and Runon nudged him amused when he saw his face. Well, it's been a long journey, even Gwyn had started to look...good. Finally, he got to see some other girls! Gwyndolin smiled happily when she saw another girl, though. She had been around those three men for two months! Bastan looked after the girl when she touched his shoulder. "Yeah...uh, thanks." Gwyndolin chuckled quietly. "Yes, all of us are very grateful." she agreed before carefully taking a sip from the bowl. "Mhh..." This was so good...so warm in the hands, the fire was drying her cold, wet skin... They all quietly sipped their soups and recovered a little from the cold. Dabble, too, sank down near the fire and Rohal leaned his back a bit against the old girl while stretching his feet into the direction of the fire.

The Altmer had to chuckle when the Bosmer asked for more money. "Well, since you can't read it, I'll take that heavy old thing off of your hands for twenty gold." he offered in return but also got a bit distracted by the nord. "Ah yes, this is Bron, he's an old drunkard and a gambler. Either someone used his state to steal from him or he is making a ruckus because he lost another of his games again." the older man said and made a dismissive gesture. "Best stay clear, the more people gather in one place, the higher the chances are you run into someone or something shady. With his troublesom character, I bet his gambling habit isn't his only bad vice." He turned back to Elluinor and smiled when he heard his excitement. "Ah, fresh out of the forest, then? Then you should visit the guilds. There is a lot of work to be done there and they hire adventures. Also, there is the Arena, if you can take a brawl. I don't visit it...too bloody for my taste." He tabbed his bearded chin and eyed Elluinor. "Say, will you be staying in Cyrodill for a little while longer?" he asked intrigued.
